body_text: Kirby Corporation Announces 2025 Third Quarter Results by Sarah Hudgins | Oct 29, 2025 | Press Releases PDF Version HOUSTON, Oct. 29, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Kirby Corporation (“Kirby”) (NYSE: KEX) today announced net earnings attributable to Kirby for the third quarter ended September 30, 2025, of $92.5 million or $1.65 per share, compared with earnings of $90.0 million, or $1.55 per share for the 2024 third quarter. Consolidated revenues for the 2025 third quarter were $871.2 million compared with $831.1 million reported for the 2024 third quarter. David Grzebinski, Kirby’s Chief Executive Officer, commented, “Kirby’s third quarter performance reflects our ability to adapt and deliver results, with continued strength in coastal marine and power generation, and focused execution in the face of softer inland market conditions.” “In inland marine, market conditions experienced near-term softness during the third quarter, primarily due to seasonally favorable weather, improved navigational conditions, a lighter feedstock mix for our refinery and chemical customers, and fewer barges undergoing maintenance across the industry. At the same time, general petrochemical customer activity remained muted with ongoing softness in the chemical industry. These factors contributed to our barge utilization averaging in the mid-80% range. On the pricing front, we observed temporary weakness in the spot market. Spot market rates declined in the low-to-mid single digits both sequentially and year-over-year while term contract renewals were flat when compared to the prior year. In the fourth quarter, we are already seeing market conditions improve and expect this trend to continue. We also continue to see constraints in long-term barge construction keeping new supply in check.” “In coastal marine, market fundamentals remained strong during the third quarter. Barge utilization levels were in the mid to high-90% range, supported by consistent customer demand and tight industry supply. Pricing continued to meaningfully improve, with term contract renewals up in the mid-teens range year-over-year. The combination of strong demand and limited vessel availability contributed to operating margins reaching around 20% for the quarter.” “In distribution and services, our teams performed well and delivered year-over-year growth in both revenue and operating income, with solid contributions across most of our end markets. In power generation, revenues increased 56% year-over-year as demand from data centers and prime power customers continued to show strength. As inbound orders accelerated, our backlog grew, and we secured more opportunities in backup and behind-the-meter power applications. In the commercial and industrial market, revenues increased 4% year-over-year, supported by consistent marine repair activity and continued improvement in on-highway service. In oil and gas, while revenues declined year-over-year due to softness in conventional activity, we achieved a 5% increase in operating income driven by strong execution, strategic cost management, and sustained execution in e-frac equipment. Overall, the segment continued to perform well, reflecting strength in power generation and our agility in responding to changing demand patterns, with total segment operating income advancing 40% year-over-year.” Contact: Kurt Niemietz 713-435-1077

title: Singapore Airlines Suites Routes, Prices, and How to Book in 2026
summary: A current guide to Singapore Airlines Suites routes, A380 aircraft, one-way KrisFlyer award prices, booking steps, and what to know before you search for Singapore Suites availability.
body_text: Singapore Airlines Suites Routes, Prices, and How to Book in 2026 By Tim Qin - Updated: June 22, 2026 A current guide to Singapore Airlines Suites routes, A380 aircraft, one-way KrisFlyer award prices, booking steps, and what to know before you search for Singapore Suites availability. Singapore Airlines Suites are one of the hardest premium cabins to pin down because they are not simply any Singapore Airlines first class seat. Suites are the airline's private A380 cabin, with only six suites on the upper deck, a separate leather chair and bed, and very limited award space. This guide focuses on the questions searchers usually need answered before booking: which Singapore Airlines A380 routes have Suites, how much Singapore Suites cost in KrisFlyer miles, how to verify the aircraft, and how to use Roame to search for first class award availability. Quick answer: Singapore Airlines Suites routes and prices Singapore Suites are available only on Airbus A380 flights. Use the route and price snapshot below as a starting point, then verify your exact flight number is still A380-operated before transferring points or ticketing. Route Service pattern Flight time KrisFlyer miles one-way Booking note Singapore (SIN) to London Heathrow (LHR) Year-round, twice daily 13 hours 141,000 A flagship long-haul option, but competition for award space is high. Singapore (SIN) to Sydney (SYD) Year-round, twice daily 8 hours 93,500 Long enough to enjoy the full Suites experience. Singapore (SIN) to Delhi (DEL) Year-round, daily 5-6 hours 58,500 One of the better practical targets for award availability. Singapore (SIN) to Mumbai (BOM) Year-round, daily 5-6 hours 58,500 Often easier than London or Sydney for finding seats. Singapore (SIN) to Auckland (AKL) Seasonal, mid-January to late March 2026 Check schedule 93,500 Seasonal A380 service can change; verify aircraft before booking. Singapore (SIN) to Shanghai Pudong (PVG) Seasonal early February to late March 2026, then year-round from May 2026 5 hours 40,500 A lower-mileage option when A380 service is loaded. Singapore (SIN) to Hong Kong (HKG) Brief five-week service in late June to July 2026 4 hours 35,000 Shortest and lowest-mileage route in this snapshot. Key takeaway: Delhi and Mumbai are shorter flights, but they are often the most realistic Singapore Suites targets because fewer travelers chase them compared with London or Sydney. Seasonal routes can be excellent value, but they require extra aircraft checks because A380 swaps remove the Suites cabin. Singapore Suites vs Singapore Airlines First Class Singapore Airlines uses two different premium labels that people often mix up. Singapore Airlines Suites are the A380 product. Singapore Airlines First Class on Boeing 777 aircraft is a separate first class cabin, not Suites. If your goal is the private Suite with the separate chair and bed, filter for the Airbus A380. The current A380 Suites cabin has six suites. The adjoining Suites 1A and 2A, or 1F and 2F, can be booked together for the double-suite setup when both seats are available. The product is still subject to aircraft changes, so a route that normally has A380 service is not enough on its own. Does Singapore Airlines first class have a shower? No. Singapore Airlines Suites do not have an onboard shower. The A380 Suites cabin instead has two spacious lavatories, including a larger lavatory with a sit-down vanity and premium toiletries. If you are comparing Singapore Suites with Emirates A380 First Class, the shower is a key difference. How to book Singapore Airlines Suites with points Unlike many premium cabins, Singapore Suites award space is primarily bookable through Singapore Airlines' own KrisFlyer program. KrisFlyer accepts transfers from major transferable points programs, including American Express Membership Rewards, Chase Ultimate Rewards, Citi ThankYou Points, Capital One, and Bilt Rewards. You can compare cards and transferable points options on Roame's credit cards page. Confirm the route has A380 Suites Start with a route known to have Singapore Airlines A380 service, then verify the exact flight shows Airbus A380 before you book. Search first class award space Search for Singapore Airlines first class space in KrisFlyer or use Roame with filters for fare class First Class, airline Singapore Airlines (SQ), and aircraft Airbus A380. Compare Saver and Advantage pricing Saver seats are the best value but scarce. Advantage awards cost more miles but can be more realistic when travel dates are fixed. Transfer points only after finding bookable space Because transfers can be irreversible, wait until you see bookable Singapore Suites space before moving points into KrisFlyer. Booking tips for Singapore Suites availability Filter by aircraft, not just cabin. A Singapore Airlines first class result on a 777 is not Singapore Suites. Use Delhi and Mumbai as practical starting points if London and Sydney have no Saver space. Check seasonal routes early and often. A short seasonal A380 window can disappear or change aircraft. For two travelers, look specifically for adjoining Suites 1A/2A or 1F/2F if you want the double-suite experience. Recheck the aircraft before departure. Singapore Airlines notes that Suites may be unavailable if there is an aircraft change. Singapore Airlines Suites FAQ Good things take time... Final thoughts Singapore Airlines Suites remain worth targeting, but the winning search strategy is specific: find an A380 route, confirm the exact aircraft, compare Saver and Advantage pricing, and stay flexible on shorter routes where award space can be easier to secure.

title: Nicola Mavilla is appointed Senior Vice-President Exploration of TotalEnergies
summary: Paris, October 6, 2025 – TotalEnergies announces the appointment of Nicola Mavilla as Senior Vice President Exploration of the Company, with effect from 1st November 2025. Nicola Mavilla is replacing Kevin McLachlan, who held this position since 2015. Nicola Mavilla has 25 years of experience in the oil and gas industry and a strong track […]
body_text: Paris, October 6, 2025 – TotalEnergies announces the appointment of Nicola Mavilla as Senior Vice President Exploration of the Company, with effect from 1st November 2025. Nicola Mavilla is replacing Kevin McLachlan, who held this position since 2015. Nicola Mavilla has 25 years of experience in the oil and gas industry and a strong track record in leading successful exploration activities. He joined Eni in 2002 and served as exploration manager in Libya and Norway, VP exploration for West Africa, VP exploration for Americas and Northern Europe and managing director of Eni Ivory Coast. Since 2024, he was Head of Exploration Projects of Eni. Nicola Mavilla holds a Ph.D. in Geology from the University of Bordeaux. TotalEnergies invests around 1 billion dollars annually in exploration and appraisal, focusing on prospects that have the potential to generate low cost, low-emissions oil and gas developments. The Company's exploration activities led to major discoveries over the past three years, notably in Suriname and Namibia. ***

body_text: Every data leader knows the challenge: AI is everywhere in your workflows, but proving its impact is another story. How much time is it actually saving your team? Which questions are being deflected instead of landing in your inbox? Who in your org is really leaning on AI, and which areas of the business are benefitting most? Until now, these answers have been hard to come by. You could guess at adoption based on anecdotal wins, but not measure it. That’s why we built AI Analytics, a new workspace-level dashboard that puts numbers behind the value of Secoda AI . With AI Analytics, you’ll see exactly how your organization is using Secoda AI , from total queries and time savings to usage trends over time, top categories of questions, and feedback from your team. It’s the clearest picture yet of how AI is driving impact across your data organization. What can you track with AI Analytics? Total queries Track the total number of queries your organization has made to Secoda AI to measure adoption and engagement. A growing query count indicates active usage and strong integration of AI into daily workflows. Total time savings Quantify how much time Secoda AI is saving your team across all workflows, whether that’s answering questions, writing documentation, or handling governance tasks. The calculation estimates total hours or minutes saved by comparing AI-assisted actions to the average time a human would spend completing the same tasks manually. This is a key indicator for demonstrating ROI and operational efficiency gains from Secoda AI. AI chats over time Visualize how AI usage evolves within your organization. Trend charts reveal peaks, dips, and long-term adoption patterns, helping you identify when and how Secoda AI delivers the most value. Use this view to measure sustained engagement or adoption following new feature rollouts or training initiatives. Prompts by member See which team members are most engaged with Secoda AI. This view highlights top users, helping you identify early adopters, power users, and potential internal champions who can help drive broader adoption and best practices. Categories of questions asked Break down usage by category to understand where AI is having the most impact. Categories include: Discovery & Search – Finding datasets, metrics, or dashboards faster Documentation & Metadata – Generating or improving asset documentation Governance & Compliance – Clarifying data ownership, access, or sensitivity Quality & Monitoring – Explaining tests, alerts, and data health metrics Automation & Workflows – Streamlining repetitive data management and business analytics tasks These insights reveal which workflows are saving the most time and where additional AI automation could add further value. Time filters for deeper insights Apply date filters to focus on usage during a specific week, month, or quarter. Use these filters to track adoption trends over time, monitor the impact of product rollouts, or report AI-driven efficiency metrics to leadership and stakeholders. Feedback from users Track real user sentiment to improve AI accuracy and adoption. The Feedback widget aggregates user interactions, showing total Likes and Dislikes alongside the specific AI chats they relate to. You can click into each response to see the conversation context and understand why it received positive or negative feedback. This helps your data team identify where Secoda AI is performing well and where prompts or context might need refinement. Why does this matter for your team? Many organizations adopt AI, but few can show its return on investment. AI Analytics changes that. It gives workspace admins clear, measurable metrics they can share with leadership to demonstrate real ROI in terms of time saved and questions deflected. This visibility also provides a pulse on how AI is being used across the organization. Admins can quickly see if adoption is uneven across departments. For example, if teams aren’t fully taking advantage of features like auto-documentation, they can step in to provide support. They can also spotlight champions who are using Secoda AI in innovative ways to solve problems faster and set the standard for others. By tracking adoption and engagement at both the team and individual level, AI Analytics helps leaders allocate resources more effectively, build trust with stakeholders, and guide their AI adoption strategy with data instead of guesswork. Getting started With AI Analytics, you can move beyond “we think AI is helping” to measurable proof of impact. Track usage, adoption, and savings, all in one place. AI Analytics is now live in your workspace. Explore your organization’s usage today to see how much time you’re saving with Secoda AI and where your team is finding the most value.

title: Performance Stories: Braking with Brembo
summary: Braking isn’t where performance ends. It’s where it begins. At Brembo’s R&D facility in northern Italy, we met Matteo Rampazzo to understand how fifty years of motorsport innovation have shaped the braking system in Polestar 4 with Performance pack.
body_text: That confidence is built into every Polestar 4 with Performance Pack. Each car comes with ventilated discs (392 × 34 mm front, 364 × 26 mm rear) and lightweight aluminium four-piston calipers, making Brembo's system ideal for precise, consistent stopping — even at high racing temperatures — while reducing weight, wear, and dust. "A great braking system doesn’t just stop fast. It stops smart," explains Matteo. In an EV like Polestar 4, integrated regenerative braking converts deceleration into energy, helping you go further between charges. In Polestar 4, this equates to well over 500km of range on a single charge (WLTP range of 590 km). So, the next time you tap the brakes in your Performance pack Polestar, remember that you're tapping into half a century of racing heritage. Engineered to perform at the highest level, the Polestar 4’s Brembo brakes don’t just stop you. They keep you ahead. Find out more about Polestar 4 with Performance pack here .

title: Better data, better decisions: Risk assessment in the open finance era
summary: Learn how open finance revolutionizes risk assessment practices for sophisticated fintech companies and banks worldwide
body_text: Risk assessment has always been at the heart of financial decision-making. However, the quality of these assessments is only as good as the data that informs them. This article explores how open finance revolutionizes risk assessment practices, drawing on Taktile's extensive experience working with sophisticated fintech companies and banks worldwide. It examines the new data streams available to teams today, how these enhance decision-making, and explores examples of open finance data being applied to onboarding, credit underwriting, and transaction monitoring use cases. Key takeaways Open finance unlocks richer customer insights, giving financial institutions access to real-time data across accounts, transactions, and institutions for more accurate risk assessment. Smarter credit underwriting is now possible, with lenders able to evaluate non-traditional applicants, personalize loan terms, and make instant, data-driven decisions. Customer onboarding is faster and safer, as verified open finance data streamlines KYC/AML checks, enables dynamic profiling, and supports personalized journeys from day one. Transaction monitoring gains a holistic view, allowing teams to detect anomalies across institutions, strengthen AML compliance, and respond to fraud in real time. Next-generation Decision Platforms like Taktile amplify these benefits, empowering risk teams to plug in open finance data, test policies, and adapt quickly to shifting risks. How open finance powers holistic decision-making Through secure open finance API connections, product and risk teams can access a wealth of information about consenting customers’ finances—far beyond what is available in their own systems. This data powers sophisticated decision-making models, giving them a more complete understanding of customers’ finances. Here is how this process works: The benefits using open finance data for risk assessments Implementing open finance data can spark a virtuous cycle of improvements for both fintech companies and banks. Imagine a fictional mid-sized bank named FMB that has recently embraced open finance data. Here are just a few benefits that a shift towards using open finance data unlocked for FMB: Enhanced customer insights and more accurate risk assessment FMB began by integrating open banking data into its risk assessment process. This allowed it to gain a more comprehensive view of its customers' financial situations. For instance, when evaluating a loan application from Sarah, a freelance graphic designer, FMB could analyze far more than just her credit score. It could also consider her consistent income from multiple clients, how she responsibly managed her business expenses, and her regular savings habits. Tailored product offerings This nuanced understanding of Sarah's finances enabled FMB to offer her a competitive small business loan, which it might have declined based solely on traditional credit data. Applying this improved risk assessment across its portfolio increased its approved application rate while unlocking a significant reduction in defaults. The success in risk assessment had a ripple effect. With more accurate risk profiles, FMB optimized its capital allocation, directing resources to promising opportunities in the freelance and gig economy markets. It also developed a suite of financial products tailored to this underserved segment, including flexible lines of credit and specialized savings accounts. Stronger customer relationships FMB used the wealth of open finance-powered data now available to create hyper-personalized customer experiences. For Sarah, this meant receiving proactive notifications about tax-saving opportunities based on her business expenses, and tailored advice on how to smooth out her irregular income. This level of personalization built trust and strengthened customer relationships, significantly increasing FMB’s customer lifetime value. Enhanced competitive advantage As these benefits compounded, the bank found itself at the forefront of financial innovation in its market. When economic conditions shifted and many traditional lenders pulled back from small business lending, FMB was able to adapt quickly, adjusting its risk models and continuing to serve its customers effectively. By embracing open finance, the bank transformed itself from a traditional lender into a dynamic financial partner for its customers. The result? A more agile, customer-centric, and profitable institution. Three examples of open finance-powered decision-making To truly demonstrate the transformative impact of open finance, we need to examine its real-world applications. This section examines three moments in the customer lifecycle where open finance is making a significant difference: customer onboarding, loan underwriting, and transaction monitoring. 1. Customer onboarding Open finance has turned customer onboarding from a necessary tickbox process into a strategic opportunity. By leveraging open finance data, teams can create a smoother, faster, and more personalized onboarding experience—satisfying regulatory requirements while also setting the tone for the remainder of the relationship. Streamline KYC and AML processes Open finance has revolutionized Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) procedures. Instead of relying on manual document checks and self-reported information, fintech companies and banks can now access verified data directly from other banks and financial service providers. For example, when a customer applies for a new account, you can, with the customer's consent, instantly retrieve their identity information, address history, and existing financial relationships from multiple sources. This approach significantly reduces the time and effort required for identity verification. What once took days or even weeks can now be completed in minutes. Plus, by cross-referencing data from multiple sources, you can more accurately detect potential fraud or money laundering risks. Enhance customer profiling Open finance enables product and risk teams to build a comprehensive financial profile of new customers from day one. By accessing transaction data from existing bank accounts, investment portfolios, and credit products, teams can gain insights into a customer's financial behavior, preferences, and needs. For instance, you might discover that a new customer regularly makes international transfers, indicating a potential need for a foreign currency account or international payment services. Or you might identify a regular savings pattern, suggesting an opportunity for investment products. This rich data allows for immediate, personalized product recommendations, increasing the likelihood of being able to cross-sell products based on a customer’s individual requirements. Undertake superior risk assessment Open finance data allows institutions to conduct a preliminary risk assessment during the onboarding process itself. By analyzing a customer's transaction history, income patterns, and existing financial commitments, you can make informed decisions about credit limits, account types, and service offerings right from the get-go.
